title: Geometry - Lesson 8 Practice: Number of Sides and Angle Sums
description: Practice using triangle decomposition and polygon angle-sum patterns.

questions.question: What formula gives the interior angle sum of an n-sided polygon?
questions.explanation: An n-sided polygon can be divided into n - 2 triangles, and each triangle has an angle sum of 180 degrees.

questions.question: What is the interior angle sum of a hexagon?
questions.explanation: A hexagon has 6 sides, so (6 - 2) x 180 = 4 x 180 = 720 degrees.

questions.question: A decagon has 10 sides. What is its interior angle sum? Enter just the number.
From one vertex, how many triangles can a pentagon be divided into?
questions.explanation: A pentagon has 5 sides, so it forms 5 - 2 = 3 triangles from one vertex.

questions.question: Find one interior angle of a regular octagon. Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: The total angle sum is (8 - 2) x 180 = 1080. Divide by 8: 1080 / 8 = 135.

questions.question: A regular polygon's total interior angle sum is divided by the number of sides to find one interior angle.
questions.explanation: A regular polygon has equal interior angles, and it has one interior angle at each vertex.

questions.question: A polygon has an interior angle sum of 900 degrees. How many sides does it have? Enter just the number.
Explain why a quadrilateral has an interior angle sum of 360 degrees.
questions.correctAnswer: A quadrilateral can be divided into 2 triangles from one vertex. Each triangle has an angle sum of 180 degrees, so 2 x 180 = 360 degrees.
questions.explanation: The explanation should connect triangle decomposition to the total angle sum.
